UK Company Administration Statistics

In June 2026 there were 191 administrations in England and Wales, 10% of all company insolvencies. Administration is a procedure run by a licensed insolvency practitioner that aims to rescue a company as a going concern, or to get a better result for creditors than an immediate liquidation. The company gains protection from creditor action while a plan is put in place. This page tracks the monthly trend back to 2000, the rate per 10,000 companies and how the procedure sits within the wider insolvency total.

Trend

Monthly UK administrations since 2000

Administration volumes are small and can swing sharply on a single event. Connected real estate companies entering administration in clusters lifted the figure three times in the first half of 2026, in March, April and June, pushing administrations across that period around 41% above 2025 levels. Read short-term moves with care.

View range

How to read this

What the administration figures show

Monthly administration volumes are small, so a single cluster of connected companies can move the figure sharply. Read month-to-month changes with care, and do not treat a single cluster as evidence of a general trend in administrations.

The count is a volume, not a failure rate. The rate per 10,000 companies is a 12-month rolling figure, not the chance of a company failing in the latest month, and it adjusts for the size of the active register.

Administrations are one procedure within the UK company insolvency statistics. See also CVL statistics and company insolvencies by sector.

Method

UK company insolvency statistics: methodology

Company insolvency data is sourced mainly from Companies House. Compulsory liquidation data for England and Wales comes from the Insolvency Service, and compulsory liquidation data for Northern Ireland comes from the Department for the Economy in Northern Ireland.

The headline England and Wales figures use seasonally adjusted data where the Insolvency Service has identified seasonality. Scotland and Northern Ireland figures are shown on an unadjusted basis.

The statistics count formal company insolvency procedures. They do not include members' voluntary liquidations, dissolutions or ordinary company closures.

Data limitations

  • The latest month is provisional and can be revised.
  • Industry is based on self-reported SIC codes.
  • Registered office addresses are not a reliable guide to where a company traded.
  • Solvent company closures are not included.
